items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I was walking around and I see the Judge, Milt Hinton, pushing his upright bass with his electric bass... So he was shocked, he said “Judge, what are you doing?”

ctx.x: After taxes. And this was before the bikes came in. I was a messenger. I was taking the subway and walking. Package was fifty cents then. Then my big job came after that, I worked with the Wall Street Journal I had two bags of newspapers. I’d get there at six o’clock in the morning and pack up my bags and so I was walking one day, I had two bags and I was going to the Pan Am building. And that was my last drop off. So that’s why I love going there because I could just drop three hundred papers. So I’m walking…
